query: Which method can be used for oxidation resistance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Stationary friction processing (SFP) enhances the oxidation resistance of AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys by refining the grain structure, which in turn promotes the formation of dense, protective oxide scales.
generation.material_initial_state: AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy in the as-cast state with coarse grains (~98 μm) and a BCC/B2 microstructure that tends to form nonprotective spinels during oxidation.
generation.intervention: Apply stationary friction processing using a WC-cylindrical tool at selected rotational speeds (e.g., 400 rpm or 1800 rpm for 5 minutes) to refine the grain structure.
generation.conditions: Isothermal oxidation in laboratory air at elevated temperatures (850 °C to 1050 °C) for extended durations (up to 100 hours).
generation.structural_mediator: Transformation from coarse-grained BCC/B2 microstructure to an ultrafine-grain (down to 0.43–1 μm) structure along with a phase transition to a higher FCC fraction and an increased surface free energy.
generation.mechanism: The refined microstructure results in a high density of grain boundaries that facilitates rapid outward diffusion of chromium ions, which form a dense Cr2O3 layer. This is accompanied by inward oxygen diffusion leading to the formation of an Al-rich inner oxide. The overall effect suppresses the formation of nonprotective spinels and decelerates the oxidation kinetics.
generation.predicted_outcome: Processed samples will exhibit lower mass gains, reduced parabolic rate constants, and predominantly protective oxide layers (Al₂O₃ and Cr₂O₃) compared to the as-cast condition.
generation.baseline: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi HEA with coarse grains showing faster oxidation kinetics, higher cumulative mass gains, and formation of nonprotective spinel phases.
generation.boundary: The expected benefits are applicable under high-temperature oxidizing conditions (850–1050 °C for durations similar to the reported 100 h tests) and may depend on the exact processing parameters such as rotational speed.
generation.uncertainty: Variability in oxidation performance may occur with changes in processing conditions, and the precise quantitative improvement in oxidation resistance might vary with the selected processing speed and duration.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a set of AlCoCrFeNi samples in the as-cast condition and identical samples processed by stationary friction processing at two different rotational speeds. Subject both sets to isothermal oxidation in laboratory air at 850 °C, 950 °C, and 1050 °C for 100 hours. Use techniques such as SEM, XRD, and mass gain measurements to analyze the microstructure and oxide phases formed in each sample.
measurements: Grain size distribution (via SEM or TEM)
Phase identification of the oxide layers (using XRD)
Parabolic rate constants of oxidation kinetics
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the SFP-processed samples do not show a statistically significant decrease in oxidation kinetics (mass gain and parabolic rate constants) or fail to form predominantly protective oxide scales (e.g., if they form nonprotective spinel phases similar to unprocessed samples), then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Paper card. Question: How does an ultrafine-grain microstructure, obtained via stationary friction processing, affect the oxidation behavior of AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy?. System: Equimolar AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy (HEA). Processing: Stationary friction processing (SFP) using a WC-cylindrical tool (12 mm diameter) at rotational speeds of 400 rpm and 1800 rpm for 5 min duration. Test conditions: Isothermal oxidation in laboratory air at 850, 950, and 1050 °C for 100 h. Findings: Grain size refined from 98 μm (as-cast) to 1 μm (SFP_400) and 0.43 μm (SFP_1800).; Phase transformation from BCC/B2 to FCC occurred, with 38% and 55% FCC fraction for SFP_400 and SFP_1800, respectively.; Surface free energy increased by 29.8% for SFP_400 and 35.2% for SFP_1800 compared to as-cast.; Oxidation kinetics decelerated by 12–20% for SFP_400 and 38–48% for SFP_1800 compared to as-cast.; Cumulative mass gain at 850 °C after 100 h was 0.33 mg/cm² (as-cast), 0.27 mg/cm² (SFP_400), and 0.17 mg/cm² (SFP_1800).; Parabolic rate constants (k_p) at 1050 °C were 23.2 × 10⁻¹³ g²·cm⁻⁴·s⁻¹ (as-cast), 18.4 × 10⁻¹³ (SFP_400), and 8.16 × 10⁻¹³ (SFP_1800).; Processed samples formed predominantly protective
